name: Stanzach
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Lechtal valley, featuring traditional Tyrolean architecture and the wild, romantic banks of the Lech river.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Stanzach is located in the Tyrolean district of Reutte (Außerfern) at an altitude of 939 metres above sea level on an alluvial cone where the Namlos stream joins the River Lech in the middle Lechtal valley. Cradled between the rugged crags of the Lechtal Alps to the south and the Allgäu Alps to the north, this peaceful clustered village has a population of around 500 inhabitants. Alongside the historic village core, the municipal territory includes the riverside hamlets of Blockau, Äule, Rain, and Sand, as well as the heritage alpine hamlet of Fallerschein. Stanzach is the vibrant centrepiece of the Naturpark Tiroler Lech: directly in front of the village unfolds the famed 'Lechzopf'—a dynamic braided river system with vast gravel banks, riparian forests, and rare pioneer flora such as the German tamarisk. As a key staging post along the Lechweg long-distance trail and the gateway into the secluded Namlos valley, Stanzach offers pure nature and alpine tranquillity along one of Europe's last wild rivers.

Geschichte

Permanent settlement in Stanzach dates back to the High Middle Ages, with its first recorded mention appearing in 1294 as 'Stanzahe', an Old High German term signifying an encampment or boundary dwelling. For centuries, village life was inextricably bound to the River Lech: while destructive floods were a constant threat, the river served as the vital economic artery for timber rafting. Intrepid local rafters transported mountain timber down the Lech to Füssen, Augsburg, and along the Danube towards Vienna. A major fire destroyed much of the settlement in April 1774. Between 1775 and 1780, celebrated court master builder Franz Kleinhans from Unterpinswang constructed the late-baroque parish church dedicated to Saint Michael the Archangel. Its interior showcases Nazarene frescoes painted by Johann Kärle and an original 18th-century high altar. In the 19th century, scarce agricultural yields forced many local youngsters into seasonal child labour in Swabia ('Schwabenkinder').

Anreise

By car, Stanzach is reached from the north via Reutte along the Lechtalstraße B198 in roughly twenty minutes. From the west, year-round access is available from Vorarlberg and the Bregenzerwald via Warth along the B198; in summer, the scenic Hahntennjoch pass road (L246) links Imst in the Inntal valley with Elmen. An exceptionally picturesque alternative is the winding Namloser Landesstraße (L21), leading from Bichlbach on the B179 Fernpass route through Berwang and Namlos directly down into Stanzach. Rail passengers travel via the Außerfernbahn line to Reutte in Tirol station or to Füssen in neighbouring Bavaria. From Reutte, VVT regional bus route 110 runs at regular intervals into Stanzach village centre, while bus line 112 connects the Namlos valley.

Tipps

The foremost attraction is exploring the Naturpark Tiroler Lech: the expansive gravel bars and riverside forests near Blockau provide ideal settings for leisurely walks, birdwatching (such as common sandpipers), and peaceful picnics beside turquoise glacial waters. Hikers cherish Stanzach as an official stop along the Lechweg trail; heading downriver, the dramatic suspension bridge at Forchach is well worth a visit. A highlight is Fallerschein, Tyrol's largest alpine cabin village: comprising more than 40 weather-worn log cabins at 1,302 metres in the Namlos valley, it is easily reached on foot and features cozy taverns serving authentic mountain cheese and cold platters. Experienced mountaineers can embark on rewarding summit ascents of the Namloser Wetterspitze (2,553 m) or the prominent Klimmspitze (2,464 m).
